newsitem.title: GERMANY: German public grain stocks at 18-year low.
newsitem.headline: German public grain stocks at 18-year low.

text.p: German intervention grain stocks totalled 990,000 tonnes at the end of September, their lowest since 1978 and compared with four million tonnes a year ago, the farm ministry said in a circular on Monday.
Of the 990,000, some 176,600 were already designated for export, it said ahead of the start of the November-May intervention buying campaign.

The state intervention board BLE bought just 1.69 million tonnes of grain in 1995/96 (July/June), compared with 3.73 million in 1994/95, as sellers sold more to tight free markets to benefit from strong prices.
Traders saw little scope for quick wheat intervention from this year's record 18.42 million tonne crop (17.70 million in 1995) because of high European demand for bread and feed wheat.
Rye from the lower 4.17 million tonne 1996 crop (4.52 million previously) also had good chances of being absorbed by the market because quality problems meant supplies would be offered cheaply.
But barley may go into intervention because the market might not find a convincing floor above the November intervention price of 230.50 marks/tonne.
